core_obligations: Derive faithfulness: assumption (1) makes the morphism surjective and flat, so the pullback functor is faithful by the preceding lemma, and only the essential surjectivity on morphisms remains (proof lines 8790-8792).

Set up two descent data over X, their pullbacks along the covering, and a morphism of descent data between the pullbacks, and display the square expressing that it is compatible with the descent isomorphisms (proof lines 8793-8812).

Prove the claim that the two composites from the fibre product of the source over itself to the target agree, by a calculation with scheme points: write the descent isomorphism on a pair of points as a swap, compute how it behaves after pullback, write the images of the points under the given morphism of descent data, and deduce equality of the two second coordinates from the commutativity of the square, using invertibility of the descent isomorphism (proof lines 8813-8852).

Descend the morphism: the base change of the source along the covering is an fpqc covering, so universal effectiveness of fpqc coverings factors the composite morphism through a unique morphism over the base whose base change is the given one (proof lines 8855-8863).

Show that the descended morphism is a morphism of descent data: the relevant square commutes after base change to the fibre product of the covering with itself, and since that base change morphism is surjective and flat, faithfulness of base change gives commutativity of the square itself (proof lines 8863-8875).
proof_roadmap: Faithfulness from surjectivity and flatness (proof lines 8790-8792).

The pointwise claim that the two composites agree, which the author invites the reader to prove (proof lines 8813-8852).
Descent of the morphism along the covering (proof lines 8855-8863).
Compatibility with the descent data, checked after base change using faithfulness (proof lines 8863-8875).
difficulty_reason: In the situation where descent data for schemes relative to a morphism X to S are compared along a morphism X' to X, the lemma asserts that the pullback functor is fully faithful provided that the single morphism X' to X is an fpqc covering and the base is unchanged (statement lines 8777-8787). Faithfulness is immediate from the surjectivity and flatness of the morphism together with the preceding lemma, so the substance is the essential surjectivity on morphisms (proof lines 8790-8792). Given a morphism of descent data over X', one has to produce a morphism of descent data over X pulling back to it, and this takes three separate steps. The first is a pointwise computation: the two composites from the fibre product of the source with itself over the source to the target agree, which the author proves by chasing scheme points through the two descent isomorphisms, writing the descent isomorphism on points, transporting the points along the given morphism of descent data and concluding that the two images agree after applying the second descent isomorphism, which is legitimate because that isomorphism is invertible (proof lines 8813-8852). The author explicitly advises the reader to prove this step rather than read it, which signals that it is not a formal consequence of the definitions. The second step is the descent of the morphism itself, which uses that the base change of the source along the covering is an fpqc covering and that fpqc coverings are universal effective epimorphisms, so that the morphism over X' factors through a unique morphism over X (proof lines 8855-8863). The third step closes the argument for morphisms of descent data rather than merely morphisms of schemes: the relevant square commutes because after base change to the fibre product of X' with itself over S it commutes, and the morphism between the two fibre products is surjective and flat, so that base change along it is faithful (proof lines 8863-8875). The claim is H3: three independent mechanisms -- a pointwise calculation, a descent along an effective epimorphism, and a faithfulness test after base change -- are needed, and the first of them is the kind of step the author himself flags as non-obvious.
